children.value: A power series may be differentiated or integrated term by term; the resulting series converges to the derivative or integral of the function represented by the original series within the same interval of convergence as the original series.
Two power series may be added, subtracted, or multiplied; the resultant series converges at least in the common interval of convergence.
One series may be substituted in another provided that the values of the substituted series are in the interval of convergence of the other series.
The power series of a function is unique, that is, there is just one power series of the form
